summary: Typhoon canceled a flight on a round the world trip, 26 hour delay
story: I am traveling around the world on a fixed schedule of eighty days with my traveling companion, Mr. Passepartout. On July 8 our flight from Hong Kong to Tokyo, from where we were to continue to Yokohama, was canceled because of a typhoon. We departed 26 hours later. I am claiming the hotel, our meals and the rebooking fee, which come to $580. I am also claiming $2,000 for a wager with members of my club in Boston, which I forfeited because the delay made me late for a stage of the journey we had agreed on. I keep precise records and every receipt is attached.

summary: Laptop bag stolen from a parked rental car
story: On August 22 I parked my rental car near Alamo Square in San Francisco to take some photos. I was gone for maybe twenty minutes. When I got back the rear window was smashed and my laptop bag was gone from the back seat. The car was locked, and I had put my jacket over the bag. I filed a police report online that evening and the rental company has the damage report. The bag had my laptop and my headphones in it.

summary: Suitcase and clothes ruined by fish sauce in the hold on the way to Hanoi
story: My suitcase came onto the carousel in Hanoi on June 9 wet through and smelling very strongly of fish sauce. Northwind's baggage desk told me a case of it had broken open in the hold beside my bag, and they wrote up a damage report on the spot. We were on our way to trek in Sapa, so the case held my sweaters, shirts, boots and socks, all bought for the trip. A laundry in the Old Quarter tried twice and then gave me the attached statement. Northwind has paid me $450. The suitcase now lives in our garage, and my wife has asked that this claim be settled before it comes back into the house.

story: On August 5 our ship crossed the Gulf of Alaska in rough weather and I was seasick. I went out to the rail on deck 7 for air, and while I was being ill over the side my upper and lower dentures went into the sea. My wife June saw the whole thing and has not let me forget it. Guest Services wrote up an incident note the same evening. I ate soup for the rest of the cruise. My dentist at home has made a replacement set and his invoice is attached.

summary: Trek to Machu Picchu canceled after breaking an ankle at pickleball
story: I was due to leave for a guided trek to Machu Picchu on August 3. On July 26 I was playing pickleball at my local courts, ran back for a lob and rolled my right ankle. The X-ray showed a fracture and I am in a walking boot for six weeks. My orthopedic doctor has confirmed in writing that a four day mountain trek is out of the question. I canceled with Andes Trails on July 27. Their terms do not refund anything inside 30 days of departure, and they have confirmed that in writing. I am claiming the full cost of the tour, which I paid in March. For the record, I won the point.

summary: Action camera stolen by a kea at Arthur's Pass
story: On July 8 I stopped at the Arthur's Pass visitor centre in my campervan. I put my action camera on the hood while I zipped up my jacket, standing right beside it, and a kea, which is a large green mountain parrot, landed on the hood, picked the camera up by its wrist strap and flew off toward the ridge with it. Two others watched from the roof, and I believe they were in on it. I asked the constable in the village about reporting the theft. He was sympathetic, but he said he could not open a file on a parrot. The ranger on duty saw it happen and wrote the attached statement. My receipt for the camera is attached.

At about 11:40 this morning I saw a kea take a small camera from the hood of a campervan in the visitor centre car park while the owner, Mr. Colin Meadows, was standing beside the vehicle. The bird flew with it toward the ridge above the village and we were not able to recover it. This happens several times each season. Ranger A. Tipene.

summary: Four hour delay leaving Houston because of a swarm of bees on the wing
story: Our flight from Houston to Cancun on July 24 left four hours and twenty minutes late because of bees. A swarm of them settled on the tip of the left wing while we were boarding, and the captain told us we could not push back until they had gone. A beekeeper was called and then was not allowed to touch the aircraft. Pest control was not allowed to spray it. So two hundred of us watched the bees through the terminal window for four hours. In the end the pilot started the engines and the bees left of their own accord, which I would have suggested at the start. My husband and I had lunch in the terminal while we waited. Meridian's letter and the receipt are attached.

story: My husband and I were taking the train down the coast from Seattle to Los Angeles, with a night in Portland on the way. Our train out of Portland on July 17 was due to leave at 2:25 in the afternoon and left at 9:50 that night. The conductor came through the waiting room and told us the locomotive had failed and that a replacement was coming down from Seattle. We had dinner at the station and bought snacks for the night. I asked Coastal Rail for a letter for my insurance and it is attached with the receipts. I am claiming $66 for the two of us.

summary: Business trip to Transylvania cut short by sickness
story: I am a real estate attorney and I traveled to Transylvania on June 3 to close a property purchase for a client, who insisted that the papers be signed in person at his castle. He was a most attentive host, though he kept unusual hours and I never once saw him eat. After ten days at the castle I had become weak and unwell, and I left in some haste by a route I would not recommend. I was admitted to a hospital in Budapest on June 14. The doctor there found me severely anemic and told me to go home, and his letter is attached. He was puzzled by two small marks on my neck, which I put down to the mosquitoes. I flew home on June 16 and lost my last four prepaid nights in Bistrita. The purchase went through, and I understand my client has since relocated.

I went to the police station near the Louvre that afternoon and they took my statement, but they said the printed report would take several days and I flew home before it was ready. summary: Decompression sickness after a scuba dive, hyperbaric treatment
story: On July 8 I did a guided wall dive in Cozumel with a local dive shop. My maximum depth was 24 meters and I followed my computer the whole way up, including the safety stop. About an hour after surfacing I had joint pain in my right elbow and shoulder and tingling in my hand. The dive shop took me to the hyperbaric clinic, where I was diagnosed with decompression sickness and treated in the chamber that evening and again the next morning. I have been diving for nine years and hold an Advanced Open Water certification. The clinic bill, my certification and the dive log are attached.

Inside it, my phone, my earbuds and my speaker spent about a minute in salt water, and none of them has worked since. summary: Walking trip to England canceled after the town demolished his house for a bypass
story: On Thursday, June 25, the town demolished my house to make way for a bypass. I never could get the hang of Thursdays. The town says the plans had been on display for nine months. They were on display in the basement of the planning office, in the bottom of a locked filing cabinet. I lay down in front of the bulldozer for most of the morning, without success. I was due to fly to England on June 29 for a walking trip, and I now have nowhere to keep my luggage, or anything else, so I canceled. I am claiming under the part of the policy about my home being made uninhabitable, which it certainly is. A friend has advised me not to panic.

On August 13 in Vancouver the wildfire smoke got bad and by the evening I could not catch my breath even with my inhaler. I went to the emergency room, where they gave me nebulizer treatments and steroids and kept me for a few hours until my breathing settled. The bill came to $780. summary: Eleven hour ferry delay leaving Piraeus for Santorini
story: Our ferry from Piraeus to Santorini on June 28 was due out at 7:25 in the morning and sailed at 6:40 that evening. The captain announced that one of the engines would not start and that an engineer was on his way from Athens with a part. The man at the ticket window told us the engineer was his cousin and would certainly hurry. Linda and I spent eleven hours at a harbor cafe whose playlist was one song. I can now sing it in Greek. We had breakfast and lunch there. The ferry company gave me the attached certificate at their office, and the receipts are attached.

summary: Knife roll and cookbook chewed by a rat at a cooking school in Paris
story: I spent the week of July 4 at a cooking school in Paris. On July 8 I came back from lunch to find that a rat had got into my bag in the students' locker room and chewed through my leather knife roll and most of my cookbook, which was a first edition of Everyone Can Cook. The school's letter is attached. In fairness to the rat, it seemed unusually interested in the cooking. I saw it again the next day near the stove, and I had the distinct impression that it disapproved of my soup.

documents.name: Letter from the cooking school
documents.content: Ecole de Cuisine Rive Gauche, Paris, July 9, 2026. We regret that on July 8 a rat entered the students' locker room and damaged belongings of Mr. Alfred Linguini: one leather knife roll, gnawed through along the spine, and one book, of which the cover and about forty pages were eaten. Neither can be repaired. Pest control attended the same afternoon.

summary: Checked bag arrived 41 hours late in Zurich
story: I landed in Zurich on the morning of August 4 for a week of meetings and my suitcase arrived at my hotel 41 hours later. I bought two shirts, underwear, socks and toiletries to get through the first two days. Northwind's report and my receipts are attached.
